4	plan:
5	  tool: deploy_compose
6	  image: apache/answer:2.0.2

13	  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
14	  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
15	  source: answer
16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔⛔⛔ ANSWER RUNS AN INSTALL WIZARD ON FIRST BOOT, AND WHOEVER LOADS THE URL FIRST OWNS THE SITE. script/entrypoint.sh runs `answer init` before `answer run`, and cmd/command.go:115-141 starts the installation HTTP server whenever /data/conf/config.yaml is missing. That server serves the setup pages and POST /installation/base-info, which sets the site name, the site URL and the ADMINISTRATOR account. On a public hostname there is nothing between the container going healthy and a stranger configuring your community. THERE IS A WAY TO CLOSE THIS AT DEPLOY TIME AND YOU MUST USE IT: see the next quirk. If for any reason you cannot, DO NOT hand over the URL, and do not leave the instance running."
18	  - "⛔⛔ CLOSE IT WITH AUTO_INSTALL, AND KNOW THAT THE VARIABLE HAS NO OFF SWITCH. internal/install/install_from_env.go:55-62 checks `len(env.AutoInstall) == 0` and nothing else, so ANY non-empty value turns auto-install on. Upstream's own .env.example ships AUTO_INSTALL=false, which ENABLES it. Set AUTO_INSTALL=true and mean it. When it runs, Answer performs the whole installation in-process at boot from environment variables, creates the administrator with ADMIN_NAME, ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD, writes the config file, and exits 0 so the entrypoint moves on to the real server. The account therefore exists BEFORE the hostname is ever reachable, which is the only shape that is safe by construction."
19	  - "⛔⛔ EVERY AUTO-INSTALL FIELD IS REQUIRED, AND ONE BAD FIELD DROPS YOU BACK ONTO THE OPEN WIZARD. This is the quirk most likely to break the deploy, because the failure is a printed line and not a crash: install_from_env.go prints `[auto-install] try to init by env fail: ...` and then starts the wizard anyway. From internal/install/install_req.go:123-133, all of these are validated: LANGUAGE, SITE_NAME (max 30 characters), SITE_URL (must parse as a URL), CONTACT_EMAIL (must be an e-mail address), ADMIN_NAME (2 to 30 characters matching word characters, dot, hyphen and space only), ADMIN_EMAIL (an e-mail address), ADMIN_PASSWORD (⛔ AT LEAST 8 AND AT MOST 32 CHARACTERS, so a 40-character generated string FAILS) and EXTERNAL_CONTENT_DISPLAY (exactly always_display or ask_before_display). Generate the admin credential alphanumeric and 24 characters and it satisfies every rule with nothing to escape. Then VERIFY with the script in the body rather than assuming: the wizard being open is silent."
20	  - "⛔ SITE_URL MUST BE THE REAL PUBLIC URL AND IT IS NEEDED AT DEPLOY TIME. It is baked into the site settings during the install and it is what Answer puts in e-mails and canonical links. Generate the dname yourself in full `answer-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so it is known before the container starts, and set SITE_URL to \"https://<that dname>\". A bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match. install_req.go:147-157 normalises the value to scheme plus host plus path, so pass the full https URL."
21	  - "USE LANGUAGE=en_US, NOT en-US. i18n/i18n.yaml lists the supported values and the only English one is en_US with an UNDERSCORE, while upstream's .env.example ships LANGUAGE=en-US with a hyphen. The install validator only requires a non-empty string of at most 30 characters, so the hyphenated value is accepted, stored, and then matches no bundle. Copying their example file verbatim is how you get it wrong."
22	  - "⛔ DATABASE: SET DB_TYPE=postgres OR IT USES SQLITE INSIDE THE CONTAINER. configs/config.yaml ships driver sqlite3 with the file at /data/sqlite3/answer.db, and install_req.go:44 accepts exactly postgres, mysql and sqlite3. ⚠️ DB_HOST TAKES HOST AND PORT TOGETHER, in one value, \"host:port\" (install_req.go:93-107 splits on the last colon and defaults the port to 5432). The other three map one to one: DB_NAME, DB_USERNAME, DB_PASSWORD. redu injects PGHOST, PGPORT, PGDATABASE, PGUSER and PGPASSWORD into the project .env and NEVER edits your compose, so the compose has to interpolate them itself, and DB_HOST has to be assembled as \"${PGHOST}:${PGPORT}\". Answer wants ONE database and creates its own tables, so no db_superuser is needed and it stays clear of the one-database-per-managed-server trap. PROVE IT AFTER BOOT, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because an absence alone proves nothing: run `sudo docker exec <container> cat /data/conf/config.yaml` and confirm the driver line says postgres and the connection names the private database VM (the positive half, which also tells you your exec command worked), THEN `sudo docker exec <container> ls /data/sqlite3` and confirm there is no answer.db. The VM runs docker, not podman."
23	  - "TLS TO THE DATABASE IS NOT AVAILABLE ON THE AUTO-INSTALL PATH, AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT THE CODE, NOT A CHOICE YOU ARE MAKING. install_req.go:68-71 builds the postgres connection string with a HARDCODED sslmode=disable whenever the Ssl flag is false, and loadEnv() never sets that flag, so there is no environment variable that turns it on. The traffic is on redu's private network between two VMs in your own project, which is why this is survivable, but say it in the handover rather than letting the user assume TLS. The connection string is written into /data/conf/config.yaml, so THE DATABASE PASSWORD IS ON THE APP VM'S DISK IN PLAINTEXT; treat that volume accordingly and never copy it into a repository."
24	  - "⛔⛔ LOSING THE /data VOLUME WHILE KEEPING THE DATABASE WEDGES THE CONTAINER ON THE INSTALL SERVER. This is read from the control flow at v2.0.2, not measured, and it is the sharpest reason /data must be a real volume. On a boot with no config file but an already-populated database: auto-install writes the config, then install_controller.go:225-228 sees the tables already exist, returns 200 and RETURNS BEFORE the os.Exit(0) goroutine at 246-249 is scheduled. install_main.go:54-61 then starts the installation server and blocks, so the app never starts. Reading the same code, a container RESTART clears it, because `answer init` then finds both the config file and the tables and returns immediately. Mount /data and the situation never arises."
25	  - "⛔ /data IS MORE THAN UPLOADS. configs/config.yaml puts the config file at /data/conf/config.yaml, uploaded images and avatars at /data/uploads, the file cache at /data/cache/cache.db and the translation bundles at /data/i18n. Postgres holds the questions, answers, users and settings; the images attached to them do not, and neither does the config that tells the app where Postgres is. Mount a volume on /data. Disk is the constraint that grows here: a community with image uploads fills the app VM, and growing it later is a volume resize rather than a redeploy, so size it with the user rather than defaulting."
26	  - "⛔ DO NOT COPY SITE_ADDR FROM .env.example. internal/base/conf/conf.go:85-89 lets SITE_ADDR override the HTTP listen address, and their example file ships SITE_ADDR=0.0.0.0:3000 while configs/config.yaml listens on 0.0.0.0:80 and the Dockerfile exposes 80. Set it and the app moves off the port you published, and the symptom is a hostname that never answers while the container looks perfectly healthy. LEAVE IT UNSET. Same for INSTALL_PORT, which defaults to 80 and only matters if the wizard runs at all."
27	  - "PORT 80, AND UPSTREAM'S OWN COMPOSE PUBLISHES 9080. Their docker-compose.yaml maps 9080:80; the compose in this file maps 80:80 and you pass port 80 to deploy_compose. If you copy theirs instead, pass 9080. Their compose also pins nothing: the image line is bare `apache/answer`, which resolves to the rolling tag. Pin apache/answer:2.0.2, which was current on 2026-08-17."
28	  - "⛔ /healthz PROVES NOTHING ABOUT WHICH SERVER IS RUNNING. Both engines register it: internal/base/server/http.go:65 for the real app and internal/install/install_server.go:57 for the installer. A green /healthz is equally consistent with a fully installed community and with an open install wizard waiting for a stranger. Worse, internal/router/ui.go:101-102 makes the RUNNING app answer 200 with index.html for any unknown path, so a status code alone cannot separate them either. Use GET /answer/api/v1/siteinfo, which exists only on the real app and returns JSON, and distinguish the installer by BODY. The script in the body does exactly this."
29	  - "REGISTRATION IS OPEN AFTER YOUR ADMIN EXISTS, AND IT IS A UI TOGGLE WITH NO ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE. internal/migrations/init.go:227-240 seeds allow_new_registrations true, allow_email_registrations true, allow_password_login true and require_email_verification true. There is no deploy-time file or variable that closes it, so if the user wants a private community the FIRST thing to do after the deploy is Admin then Login then turn off new registrations. The anonymous GET /answer/api/v1/siteinfo reports the current state under login.allow_new_registrations, so you can check it from outside without credentials. Ask the user which they want and set it deliberately."
30	  - "THE SITE IS PUBLICLY READABLE, BY CONSTRUCTION ON THIS PATH. install_from_env.go:64-82 never populates LoginRequired, so the env install always writes login_required false into the security settings and every question, answer, user profile and ranking is readable anonymously. That is the right default for a Q&A community and the wrong one for an internal knowledge base. The toggle is Admin then Security then Login required, and it is also readable anonymously from siteinfo. There is also a check_update flag defaulting to true (internal/migrations/init.go:242-249); what it calls was not traced here, so if the user wants no outbound calls at all, turn it off and confirm from the VM rather than trusting this sentence."
31	  - "NO SMTP MEANS NO PASSWORD RESET AND NO USABLE PUBLIC SIGNUP. Answer seeds an empty e-mail configuration and requires e-mail verification for new accounts, so on a fresh deploy a stranger can register and then never receive the verification message. Your own admin account is created directly by the installer and is not affected. If the community is meant to be open, wire Admin then SMTP to a provider the user owns before announcing it. THERE IS A RECOVERY PATH FOR A LOST ADMIN CREDENTIAL, which is unusual and worth knowing: `sudo docker exec -it <container> answer passwd -C /data/ --email <address>` prompts interactively. Upstream's own help warns that the -p form lands in shell history, and it would also be visible in ps, so use the prompt."
32	  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. The entrypoint runs `answer upgrade` on every boot after `answer init`, and the installer creates the schema. Do not add your own migration step."
33	  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO NUMBER. Checked the README, the Dockerfile, the compose and configs/config.yaml: there is no RAM or CPU figure anywhere. m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB) is reasoning from a Go binary with an embedded React build that also resizes avatars and uploaded images server-side, plus 40 GB of disk for those uploads. m1.small might well be enough for a quiet community; measure it on your run and write the real figure back, because that is the most useful thing a first deploy can add here."
34	  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.045/hr, roughly GBP 33 a month; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and doubles the bill), port 80. plan_deploy will want to upsize a compose stack to m1.large once needs_compose is declared; nothing here is built from source, so pass the flavor explicitly."

Your .env survives: redu APPENDS its PG lines to the project .env and never truncates it."
